text_fidelity_a:
OGIO Corp City [[VIDEOID:fbaddcf27c139f6513397e4ac2d8e8a0]] I love this Ogio bag! It's probably the most functional thing that I own. I'm on my second Ogio City Corp bag, because I loved the first one so much. And, the first one took four years of daily pounding, many airplane flights, literally tons of books, computers, and other things being hauled all over everywhere.

This bag has tons of pockets, and they're all extremely accessible. I love how easy my laptop is to remove when I'm taking a flight and they make me take it out of my bag. I can cram loads of stuff into this bag. This bag will get too heavy far before it gets too full. I think that it says it carries a 17" laptop, but I'm sure you could get a 19" laptop in here if you're fine with a tight squeeze.

Like I said, my first one of these bags wore out after 4 years of daily use. The reason it wore out is that there was a ton of pressure on the zipper from opening it under strain with a lot of heavy stuff in it. If you take better care of your bag than I did, you could expect this to last 10+ years of daily use.

Pros:
+Has tons of pockets. I didn't even have time on my video to go over all of the pockets and features.
+It took me over four years of daily heavy use to wear out the zipper on my first one
+Extremely high quality
+Great for a travel bag for the airplane. It's very easy to take my laptop out.
+Shoulder strap is very comfortable, even for long distance walking

Cons:
-One of the pockets has a bottom zipper, and it sometimes comes unzipped
text_fidelity_b: OGIO Corp City

text_fidelity_a: CamelBak Eddy Kids Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Bottle 12 oz,  Stainless My husband and I have used Camelbak bottles for over 15 years, and we both still use our insulated stainless bottles that are 9 years old. Our kids have been using the camelbak kids bottles for the past 2 years, and while I don’t believe a perfect kids water bottle exists, these are my favorite option. The main problem I’ve seen with camelbak kids bottles is that my 2 and 3 year old chew on the bite valve, which cause it to split wider than it should, then drip when the valve is open and it’s laying on its side. I have probably purchased 8 replacement bite valves for their bottles in the past 2 years because they only seem to last us 6 months or so before the leaking gets out of control. Thankfully Amazon sells 4 packs of replacement valves. If your kid is older and doesn’t chew on it as much, or even if they shut the valve after taking a drink, then that shouldn’t be an issue. Overall I like the camelbak design and I can clean it really well using a bottle brush and straw cleaner. As far as this stainless option goes, it is obviously more prone to being dented and banged up. We already have a nice gouge in the side after being dropped from 2 feet on to tile. But it will keep drinks cold for pretty much the whole day if you give it a few cubes of ice, and there won’t be condensation on the bottle. I love that I can put ice in this and not worry about it making a condensation puddle on my coffee table! I will happily take the dents in exchange for cold water all day long.

text_fidelity_a:
EASYANT Tactical Bushcraft Survival Kit 14 in 1 Tins for Camping Hiking Adventures Outdoor EDC Gear Kit Wow..!! You’re looking at a small sized all-inclusive survival kit that really packs a punch! For the sake of not being redundant and listing included items (see photo I used with the list!) This kit albeit tiny in stature, really holds those basic “urgent” items.. just like circus clowns fit in a toy car!! The overall footprint is perfectly small!! No bigger then, a standard 3x5 notecard- Which makes it a great option to easily tuck inside your gear bag, backpack, tackle box, car glovebox, prepper supplies, etc. Best part of all, when added to a bag- this is so light, you won’t even know it’s there! Mission accomplished.

Love the container- its reminiscent of an old fashion sardine can but, with a useable lid to keep it securely closed.. Fact- the container itself is a working piece to this kits overall function! Giving a lot of thought into keeping this minimal. Of course, being this small in size- you should expect this is just for emergent necessities. This couldn’t sustain a person more than a crisis and certainly wouldn’t suffice for multiple people needs. Items included come in increments of x1 (bandaids = x5) So, if traveling in a group for more then a day.. I’d suggest a larger kit or, at the very least supplement this one.. This has the ability to get you out of a tight spot and would say that’s it’s intended purpose!

Note: One thing I’d definitely recommend with this kit.. and can’t stress enough- is including a simple how too handbook or, guide sheet to take with Ha! Starting a fire with flint isn’t like flicking a switch! If emergent scenario.. it’s safe to assume, the situation is not ideal! So, if ever found in position to use.. it makes sense to have that helpful 411. It may be difference of life/death. (Wow.. I sounded like Dirty Harry just then- ha ha..!!)

If you are prepping for serious situations that could present in your circumstances.. One must also acquire a full first aid kit, food/water supply, Shelter- to subsidize an item like this. BUT, hopefully that is common sense if you’re truly thinking through being prepared!

A few simple adds to make this more complete: Safety pin, small bic lighter (bc, I saw in a post- fire is harder to start then, one might guess- oh, wait.. that was me!) I clipped onto this case a carabiner with a built-in flashlight!! Just those few little items can beef this up a bit. (would have loved to see them included with the set.)

Overall, this is made to avoid being caught empty-handed and could definitely step up to that task 100%. At this price point- this is a great gift for those who love to venture out into situations where they may find themselves needing to be prepared- this will do just that!! I hope this info can help in your decision.. feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: EASYANT Tactical Bushcraft Survival Kit 14 in 1 Tins for Camping Hiking Adventures Outdoor EDC Gear Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Terrain D.O.G. Elevation Harness, Medium, 3/4" x 16"-25", Sky Blue/Silver/Purple Super, high quality harness with size adjustments on ALL straps. The buckles & clasps are all constructed of plastic, but still very durable. The material used for the harness looks to be thick nylon or composite. I might even say it's a little too stiff. But again, this speaks towards the quality of the product.

I had no issues getting it on our pup (Yorkie mix) & he didn't mind it at all.

The one caveat here is that that this is a REAR CLIP harness. If you (or your fur kid) is not used to a rear clip harness, then please be aware. Especially if he or she is used to a front or middle clip.

As with front or middle clip, your pup can be pulled back or away from a dangerous or unwanted situation. You can still do that with a rear clip, but he/she won't respond to the tug. So you won't be able to "steer" for lack of a better term. Basically, it would be like turning them butt first!

I believe the rear style clips are more suited for situations where your guy has a little more freedom to walk, jump or run, but you still want the harness in place. This way you can intervene & keep keep them from hurting themselves (IE: if he or she jumps, & the leash gets stuck, they are not hanging by their neck on the harness!)

So, In my opinion, not the best style harness for daily walks that require more control. However, if your needs are more for recreation or hiking or situations where you pup has more freedom, then this harness is a great solution.
text_fidelity_b: Terrain D.O.G. Elevation Harness, Medium, 3/4" x 16"-25", Sky Blue/Silver/Purple

ProsourceFit Yoga Mats 3/16” (5mm) Thick for Comfort & Stability with Exclusive Printed Designs I must admit that I have a bit of an obsession with yoga mats. Although I have an absolute favorite mat that I use regularly (a [[ASIN:B00IOT7Y1C Manduka eKO Lite Mat]] in green, my favorite color), and several others that I use for different purposes, I can't seem to resist trying new ones. I was particularly interested in this mat because I have never tried a mat from the ProSource brand.

This mat arrived rolled in a large box. Upon opening it, I found the mandala design very appealing, although I was less enamored with the pink color--I DO like pink, but unfortunately, this is somewhat of a Pepto Bismal shade. I also detected a scent that I've found to be common to new yoga mats, especially those made of more eco-friendly materials; to me, the fragrance is reminiscent of a plastic toy for a swimming pool. This scent was NOT as strong as some other new mats I have received, and it dissipated significantly when I left the mat lying out unrolled for several days. (For other mats, I have had to leave the mat lying out in the sun to get rid of the smell.)

The ProSource mat is 5mm, thicker than many average mats that are only 3mm. However, I found it to still feel quite lightweight. (I believe that it is lighter than my Manduka eKo Lite, which is only 3mm but very dense and high quality.) I was also extremely impressed with the stickiness of this mat. Virtually EVERY yoga mat that I have every tried (with the exception of my eKo Lite) has produced some sliding, particularly when my hands are on the mat for downward facing dog, but this mat kept both my hands and feet in place.

So far, I am quite happy with the performance of this mat. For the appearance, I would knock my rating down to 4 1/2 stars (I think I would have preferred the "Mandala" option, which has the mandala design but in a much more attractive teal blue color), but I would definitely recommend his ProSource yoga mat.

text_fidelity_a:
Schwinn Trailblazer Double Bicycle Trailer We purchased this trailer for our 5 year old son to ride in on family bike rides for the next year or so. We spent a few minutes breaking it down and putting it back together in the store, and it was easy and quick to fold up and to set up again. The quick-release on the wheels is what sold us, made of metal, not plastic like others in this price range. The coupler fit easily on my husband's bike, and the trailer can be swapped to another bike in under a minute if the other bike has a coupler (additional couplers can be purchased, they're universal to the Schwinn/Instep trailers). I like that we can remove the stroller handle completely, we'll put this away for future use. The front wheel can be removed as well, or folded 90 degrees to be out of the way. Plenty of storage for picnic supplies or beach gear behind or under the seat.

The seat is a sling, and our son fits well inside, even with a helmet on and the canopy over him. He's 45" tall, and weighs 45 lbs. His posture isn't upright in the seat, he's kind of slouched down with his knees up in front of him, but he says it's fine and he's happy. We're probably going to add some rigid foam to the underside of the seat so that he might sit up a little better. We had used a different trailer (CoPilot) while on vacation, and the seat was a bit more sturdy, but we were able to find this trailer model locally at half the cost of the copilot. We plan to use this trailer for another year or so until our son is able to keep up on his own 2 wheels a little better. I wouldn't even consider putting two kids in this unit, as the sling seat would cause the children to end up in the middle squished together like in a hammock. I don't think it would be very comfortable for two, although the width of the trailer would accommodate two toddlers easily.

The fabric is rather thin polyester canvas with vinyl windows and nylon mesh screening. The seat belts are 1" webbing, they will work for us, but if you're planning to use this for years to come, you might wish to replace it with something sturdier. We had a problem with one of the buckles not staying latched on the canopy. I replaced the buckle with another one. We plan to use this trailer as a beach buggy when we're on vacation once our son outgrows it, so we aren't concerned with how thin the canvas is. I would have looked for a sturdier fabric if we planned to use this as a coach for our son for more than a year or so.

My son cannot easily undo the canopy from inside the trailer. I leave one bottom corner unsnapped so that he can pull the velcro apart by himself. The vinyl rain window rolls up once the canopy is attached. There's a back window that is mesh, with a roll-up fabric cover. The canopy can be completely removed if you wish, but the child could get sprayed with dirt or gravel coming off the rear bike tire, so be aware if that seems to be a problem. For us, it isn't.

My husband says he can't tell the trailer is there unless he's going up or down a hill. It's easy to push with the stroller handle attached, although the stroller front wheel attachment rattles while using it. I wouldn't recommend trying to use this as a stroller very much. If walking at a fast pace, you would need lift the stroller up and use just the back wheels. It would be fine for going short distances or shopping/browsing, although the width would make it difficult to maneuver in crowds. The frame is sturdy and the wheels are well made, we can find tires to replace these with if they get worn out. The ride is adequate for my son, but this isn't the luxury ride that might be expected on a higher end unit.

I was impressed with Schwinn / Pacific Cycle's customer service. The flag to our trailer was missing when we purchased it, so I called the customer service number in the directions. After a few questions about which model I had purchased, they promptly sent out a replacement.

Overall, this is a decent and safe trailer for occasional use. It's lightweight, tracks well behind the bike, is comfortable enough for short rides and my son loves it. Just don't expect a high-end bike trailer for this price, and you won't be disappointed.
text_fidelity_b: Schwinn Trailblazer Double Bicycle Trailer

Delorme West Virginia Atlas This atlas is a "must-have" for anyone wishing to explore the state of West Virginia. It is a hefty atlas, with almost as many pages as a national road atlas. This is because the state is broken down into 63 pages that depict in great detail what there is to be found there.

The first page shows the entire state, along with the major roads and cities. This map is broken into rectangles, each of which represent one page in the atlas. You can use this map to get oriented and to find the page you wish to examine in greater detail. There is also a legend, which depicts the symbols and details of the map, along with some information about the design of the atlas.

Next is a comprehensive listing of place names and map features. There are charts that list points of interest along with their map coordinates so that you can find them. These include national lands, state lands, scenic drives, unique natural features, bicycle routes, historic sites, covered bridges, etc.

When you enter the map portion of the atlas, the first thing you notice is the topographic features. Mountains and valleys, rivers and lakes all stand out so as to be easily identified. If you look closely, you can actually see the topographic lines faintly drawn on the map. All roads, down to the dirt access roads are depicted, and every town is shown. And there are symbols marking the points of interest.

West Virginia is a wild and mountainous state with much to offer the traveler and adventurer, and this map makes the ideal companion for anyone who wishes to explore the state in greater detail.
text_fidelity_b: Delorme West Virginia Atlas

Withings Go | Activity & Sleep tracker I spent hours trying to get this Nokia Health Mate Go ("Nokia") to work.

Bottom line: This is a worthless piece of junk.

Here is what I did:

1. I installed the Nokia on my iPhone 5c with associated app. The app indicated that it recognized the Nokia.
2. I put it on my left wrist and walked all over my house to test its pedometer's accuracy in counting steps. After ten minutes, it still registered zero steps. Clearly it did not record or update steps properly.
3. I tried to figure out why the device, in this regard, was not communicating well with the iPhone app. I finally employed the computer programmer's tried-and-true cure-all: I did the nearest to a "reboot" that I could. I killed the app and then restarted it.
4. I started walking again, and it was at least trying to record the steps. But all it did was state, "Looking for your tracker...."
5. Finally the app updated, and then it started to finally count steps. I then killed the app and started it again to refresh it.
6. I did a test. I walked while counting my steps myself, speaking them out loud. After 165 steps, I looked down at the Nokia. It said I had taken 55 steps.

This thing is a bust as a pedometer, and I couldn't figure out anything else it is useful for. Of all things, it can't even measure the heart rate.

This is NOT a cheaper alternative to a Fitbit. It is not good for anything. If you want a pedometer, I suggest buying one.
text_fidelity_b: Withings Go | Activity & Sleep tracker

MIER Extra Large Waterproof Duffel Backpack Roll Top Duffle Bags for Men Women 60/100/150L Heavy Duty Dry Bag for Kayaking Boating Camping Gear Motorcycle Trips Hiking Travel Rafting I received the Mier 60L backpack and immediately put it to use on my electric kick scooter. First I transported a huge load of dirty linen for my wife from her massage therapy business to the laundry via scooter (3/4 capacity). Then I swung by Trader Joe's supermarket and loaded up at least 30 lbs of food and scootered home (2/5 capacity).

The Mier backpack performed extremely well. The 60L volume is HUGE. Huuuge. I am 6' tall, 215 lbs, fit. This is ALL you need for standard transport. The 150L (at more than double the volume of the 60L) should be able to hold a body... A use for the 150L would likely be transporting bulky, light loads (e.g., 25 food trays that need to be kept vertical).

These are truly MEGA packs.

If you're working for a food delivery service, and need to use a backpack, this is your product. Super dense, sturdy material. Good strong shoulder straps with reinforced connection points. Padding on the straps is decent for usage in 30 minute stints under max load or all day under light loads. And while not officially listed as insulated, the thickness and type of material makes me think this would be good for food delivery as it should keep in the heat, keep out the cold, and be very easy to keep clean.

The only downside was my back sopping with sweat due to the pack exterior not being made of breathable material.

Highly recommended.

text_fidelity_a: Franklin Sports Full Size Hard Court Portable Basketball System My teenagers have been wanting a basketball hoop for a while. This one seems to be a nice quality one. First of all, we did not receive any instructions. My husband went to the Franklin Sports website and ended up contacting them. They emailed him a PDF with the instructions within a short time. It came with a couple of little wrenches to put it together, but my husband used his own socket set which made it a little easier. He put it together by himself, but he said it would definitely be easier with a second person. You can adjust the height, but it's not something you would do frequently. Some others have a lever that you can use to change the height. This one requires you to unscrew the screw and then adjust the tube (within a tube - telescoping). It's kind of like the pop up tents, except instead of the button you have to press, you have to unscrew the screw. It would be much easier to have a second person to help you if you are changing heights.  My husband found it easier to put the whole thing on the side to adjust the height. There are wheels on the bottom of the base so you can move it if needed. We have a two door garage and have it placed against the brick between the doors. It fits well and doesn't interfere with our cars.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Full Size Hard Court Portable Basketball System

The socks are knee high and fit a size 12 foot and medium calves with a bit of room to spare. The material is very soft and comfortable and I didn't get any binding, I also noticed less bunching up in the foot area. The heat is indeed all over and feels nicely even. Including a second pair of just socks was really smart. Aside from the inevitable wet foot, being able to charge while wearing makes it more practical to run 2 sets of socks with 1 set of batteries.
I really like the design for the battery packs, having a small button on the battery is a lot less likely to be accidentally pushed than the typical big rubber button on the outside. Battery info is also well displayed and simple - blue is temp and green is battery life.
I especially like that these are charged with standard USB-C so that I don't need to worry about having a special adapter with me. The batteries also seem to support pass through charging, so you can run cords from battery packs to get more use in one outing while also charging up the packs. Starting from full and running half the time on low and half on medium-low, I got about 9hrs before they died.
FYI - most heated socks I've seen on Amazon are rated about 7.4V, whereas these are rated like battery packs (3.7V), so the amperage ratings can seem like more than it is - 5Ah (5000mAh) at 3.7V is 18.5Wh; whereas the average 7.4V battery is around 2.5Ah (2500mAh) which is also 18.5Wh. So despite the much higher mAh rating, these have no more energy than most any other heated sock.
text_fidelity_b: Heat Socks for Women Men with 5000mAh Power Bank, 2 Pairs Rechargeable Electic Heated Socks with 4 Levels Heating Socks, Winter Warm Socks for Outdoor/Sports/Huting/Fishing/Camping

Mountain House Chicken & Dumplings | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food |2 Servings I've had a number of these lately, testing out the different flavors to see what I would like to have in the family camping and emergency supplies stash. I have been continually surprised at how good the flavors are, and how much I enjoy eating these.

The gravy mix is at the bottom, so what you do to prepare this is you measure out your boiling water carefully and pour it in, give it a stir and close the container, wait a few minutes as specified on the package, stir and close the container again to let it finish soaking in.

In my experience, the meals rehydrate best when they are made with extremely hot boiling water, and when you make sure that you do not in any way skimp on the liquid component. I measured sloppily on one of mine, and the biscuits came out a little crunchy. I have also noticed that for my personal tastes, I prefer a longer wait time than they specify. At the beginning of my meal, the center of some of the larger chunks were not fully rehydrated, and though we were all okay with the tiny bit of crunch, the meal tasted much more like a normal meal when we were almost at the end of eating it. I was worried about letting it set too long to where it got soggy, but that didn't occur, it just got tastier with a longer soaking time.

As for the flavor of this one specifically, they really got the seasonings just right. It feels like a very comforting, homemade meal, with a nice thick chicken gravy pulling together all of the chunks.
text_fidelity_b: Mountain House Chicken & Dumplings | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food |2 Servings

The different carrying cases have never lived up to the expectations or sometimes harsh environments my beloved camera has.

This Thule bag is surprisingly well made and much bigger than my best case. (See the photo for side by side comparison) This bag holds my camera and a portable tripod with some finagling of the included padded pieces. Those pieces are designed with Velcro to fit and attach in whatever shape or spot you need - which means you aren't limited to using only items that fit in pre-made pockets.

Conceivably, you could hit the trail with just this bag carrying your camera stuff, a bottle of water, your id & keys and maybe a light, small snack. I have had this out at the barn & a horse show for photos of the horses and it works fine, but it will take some time to get used to the bulk of this bag for trekking through a jungle or climbing ruins in Central America or Asia.

Best Choice Products 48in Competition Sized Foosball Table, Arcade Table Soccer for Home, Game Room, Arcade w/ 2 Balls, 2 Cup Holders - Light Bown [[VIDEOID:678ae8e2c0788b1d6c2758fadc4c938e]] [[VIDEOID:511da113ad3a77e94b62885a75944410]] I received this foosball table from the manufacturer at no cost for evaluation, and here are my thoughts.

This foosball table is made of fiberboard with an attractive wood veneer, and it's very sturdy once assembled. The directions are pretty clear, but instructions for some parts are sketchy. Be sure to refer to the picture on the product page and play close attention to the direction the players are facing so you don't install them facing the wrong way as I did. If you do that you'll have to unscrew the players and switch them around the right way and reinsert the rods again, (which is what I had to do since I messed up).

Everything fit together well in the kit I got except for the holes for the counter screws which weren't fully drilled, so I drilled them the rest of the way and was then able to install the counter. I needed a helper to hold the sides in place until the end pieces were attached, but was otherwise able to do it myself and it took less than two hours to assemble.

Once assembled, the table is sturdy, steady, and level side to side and front to back. It looks good enough to go in any room you want to put it in, and it functions well. The players stand upright properly, the rods move smoothly allowing for good playing action, and the ball catchers and counters all function well. The table is the perfect height for both adults and my 10 year old and her friends to play, and we're all getting plenty of fun out of it. All in all, this is a great foosball table for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Best Choice Products 48in Competition Sized Foosball Table, Arcade Table Soccer for Home, Game Room, Arcade w/ 2 Balls, 2 Cup Holders - Light Bown

2PCS Yellow LED Flash Tyre Wheel Valve Cap Light for Car Bike bicycle Motorbicycle Wheel Light Tire Light for Night Safety by TheBigThumb I initially bought this product because of the pictures and how it resembled a constant glow like in the movie TRON. I already was warned in the reviews that the product so not continuously stay on which was fine, with the cheap price it was a risk worth taking. Now that being said, when I received the product, I it not immediately obvious which light is what color. I had to set it up which was simple and test it out. These lights are motion activated with very low sensitivity, so the bumbs will need to be frequent or near constant in order for them to light up. Becuase these lights are on a wheel and the force exerted on the lights moves in a circular motion, the lights will not light up just because the wheel is spinning but rather when the tire hit a strong enough resistance in the road or rocks or gaps in the sidewalk. These lights probably wouldn't light up on a wheel that is operating on a smooth enough track or road. I tested it on my bike and the "blinking" lights were cool from a first person point of view, I have yet to test the "coolness" factor of the lights from a third person perspective (or in other words I am not geting any positive feedback from passer's by. I did not test this product on my car or on a motor cycle (like in the packaging).

With all that said, the price was low enough, the product was plastic, was shinny enough, and the performance is adequate. Overall the product is worth the risk! for cyclist or bike enthusiasts. text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ-720ITC Pocket Pedometer with Health Management Software I have used a few different Omron pedometers in my day and like other consumers, I purchased this one due to the solid reviews. Anything with an overall rating as good as this product should be worth the money. So, with my old pedometer on the fritz, I decided it was time for a new one and purchased this model.

Omron Pocket Pedometer was okay at first. It does measure your total steps, aerobic steps, time, calories burned, and distance. The accuracy seems to be pretty good and I like that I can monitor my progress and check things online with the software. These are all good qualities and they earn the product some respectability.

Where this product loses some points with me is with its cumbersome display; its tendency to go blank; and the lack of any ability to shut it off. With the display, what I don’t like specifically is the annoyance with looking at your statistics from past days. It stores up to a week’s worth of data, which is great, but if you want to view the data from a past day, you have to toggle back and forth between two of the buttons. You can’t just simply go back to the day you want and then view the steps, aerobic steps, time, distance, and calories with one push. You have to push the button to the left a couple of times, then push the button on the right to view one stat, then push the button on the left a couple of times again to view the next stat, etc. Other pedometers are much easier than this.
Another problem is with the tendency of the screen to go blank. This happens to me anytime I drop the pedometer. I have to then get a small screwdriver to remove the back, move the battery around, and screw it back on. The display will them reappear. And, of course, there is the problem with inability to shut the pedometer off. With other pedometers, you can turn it off or it will shut off itself after a certain amount of time has elapsed. It doesn’t work that way here. The display is always on, draining the battery at a fast rate. Sure, you could pop out the battery after each use, but this is too much trouble. Just make sure you have plenty of replacement batteries on hand because you’re going to need them.

So, taken as a whole, this is device is not as good as I expected and I plan to search for a replacement very soon. It’s disappointing for something from Omron. I have had better luck with other pedometers from this company and cannot give this one a recommendation for the reasons cited.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-720ITC Pocket Pedometer with Health Management Software

I am not going to repeat the product specs on this page since the material and unfolded dimensions are provided by the manufacturer. I will give my take on this and reasons why I rated it so highly.

What I especially like is the compact size that it folds to. Out of the box it's only 12.5x4x1 inches, which will fit in a backpack or even in the glove box of most vehicles (especially if you fold it over lengthwise.)

There is a slight chemical odor as soon as you unbox it, so I recommend airing it out before refolding and storing it for actual use. It takes about an hour for the odor to dissipate.

Using it is as simple as placing your valuables inside, folding over the reinforced rib at the top (the mouth) of the bag two or three times, then doubling and using the closure snaps. You are NOT supposed to press the air out because that will provide buoyancy in the event that it falls into water. I am not sure how much weight it will take to achieve negative buoyancy, but partially filled with air it will support a good five pounds and still maintain a degree of positive buoyancy. The key point and why I rated this so highly is I tested it with a towel and a brick and it kept the towel completely dry.

If you camp, boat or spend time at the beach and want to safeguard wallets, phones and tablets, this bag will do the trick.

text_fidelity_a:
Exerpeutic 400XL Folding Recumbent Exercise Bike We just got this bike a few days ago and so far I love it. The seat is adjustable for distance away from the pedals for taller vs. shorter. I'm 5'1" and I don't even have it on the closest distance, so someone at least a few inches shorter than me would be able to use this bike with no problem. I can sit all the way back on the seat without straining to reach the pedals at all.

It was easy to set up the bike too. There were two of us but it wouldn't be too hard with just one. There were a few pieces that were loose but most of the bolts and washers and nuts were already screwed into the various pieces you had to put together. It took maybe a half hour to assemble.

I like the bike because the seat is very wide and comfortable. I was worried my rear-end would be too wide to use the handlebars well but that isn't even close to being a problem (5'1" and 200 lbs so not a small rear-end!).

I also like the fact that there are 8 resistance settings so it'll be easy to work my way up. I can pedal while reading and it's completely silent so watching tv isn't a problem either.

There is a heart rate monitor, calorie count, timer, distance, AND odometer. Everything except the odometer is reset every time you press the button. Some people don't like it how the odometer isn't reset, but that's what the "distance" feature is for. It gives you mileage just like the odometer but that way you can keep track of how far you've gone instead of trying to remember where you started on the odometer.

Since it's only been a few days, writing the review is a little premature. If any negative issues come up I'll update my review here.

Update 1/23/2013: So two weeks after I got the bike I already had my first [small] problem. The odometer reset itself, twice. It's not supposed to reset unless you take the batteries out so I don't know what its problem was. I've used the bike a few times since then and it hasn't reset itself, so maybe it's a random thing. I hope it doesn't keep doing it because then it'll just be like two "Distance" modes.
text_fidelity_b: Exerpeutic 400XL Folding Recumbent Exercise Bike

Cressi Italian Boutique Collection - Tempered Glass Lens Frameless Scuba Snorkeling Dive Mask - Splash Guard Dry Snorkel Set Pros:
-Comfortable on face
-Straps are easily adjustable

-Dry snorkel keeps you from breathing in water if used properly...water will always find a way down your throat into your lungs
-If water does find it's way into the snorkel, it's easy to purge it

Cons:
-If you don't have a tall nose, it might be hard to squeeze to pop your ears
-Nose area could use a more flexible plastic to make the aforementioned problem less of a problem

Recommendation:
-Prep the mask before you use it for the first time by rubbing toothpaste on both sides of the lens and rinse with water, this will remove the protective film it came with. It might be a good idea to do it a couple of times.
-Right before entering the water, wet the mask and rub dish detergent on the inside of the lens and rinse again. This will keep it from fogging while you are underwater.

Backyard Champs Disc Jam Flying Disc Game I first played can jam (aka Kan Jam) with DIY cans and Frisbees. I didn't even realize it was something people bought, and it sure was fun. This replicates that experience or rather it replicates the Kan Jam game. As with all variants, its easy to learn and makes for great backyard fun for parties and gatherings. Most folks have some level of Frisbee skills, and most folks have played a game with a goal/goalie. This piggy-backs off of that common knowledge.

While the game is fun, the parts in this kit are basic. This helps keep the cost down and keeps it highly portable. text_fidelity_a:
Aosom Youth Scooter, Teens Kick Scooter, Adjustable Handlebar Ride On Toy for 5+ w/Front and Rear Dual Brakes Inflatable Wheels UPDATE: On the 3rd time riding this scooter, the brakes malfunctioned and one whole brake pad actually ripped off. This very well could have been our fault because there are not detailed instructions on the brakes. I contacted the company to try to get a replacement brake piece. I think there was a language barrier and we couldn’t get the customer service rep to understand the problem even when photos were sent. To my total surprise, they ended up sending us a brand new scooter. I misunderstood and thought they were only sending the one part so this was quite the surprise. I’m very happy about this because now we have a whole scooters worth of replacement parts.

Original Review:
Overall this looks like a nice scooter and should do my son for a while. The first thing we did was remove the tacky stickers from it and it immediately looked more expensive. The instructions that came with it are the absolute worst instructions I have ever seen. They do not include a list of parts, a list of tools needed or actually describe the steps. We are handy people, I assemble things all the time with very little effort. I've assembled many bicycles and scooters in the past. The video was useless as to how to install the handlebars, it only covered brakes and had only cheesy music, no actual verbal instructions so you had to kind of guess what the guy was doing. The guy in the video was using tools that were not included nor listed as needed for the job. The videographer also did not zoom in when he should have to show the small details. It took us 10 times longer than it should have to get this thing put together because the directions suck so bad. It's too bad because I would have given this 5 stars if there were even halfway decent instructions. It is a nice scooter especially for the price but be prepared to get extremely frustrated with the assembly.

4 cubes butter, softened
2 heaping cups dark brown sugar (packed, then heap that shiz)
½ cups white sugar
2 tablespoons vanilla
1 ½ teaspoon salt
1 ½ teaspoons baking soda
3 eggs
6 cups flour
1 bag chocolate chips (semi-sweet or sweet)

Seaview 180 Degree Panoramic Snorkel Mask- Full Face Design,Panoramic Teal,Large/Extra Large [[VIDEOID:3a1d0e8884973fd7767817b61417e9f7]] I've been snorkeling a few places around the world and I've learned just enough to know that good gear and good locations make all the difference.

I've had the chance to try out the Seaview 180 snorkeling mask from Wildhorn Outfitters. The Seaview 180 is different type of snorkel mask. The mask fits around your entire face - covering your eyes, nose and mouth.

I've experienced snorkeling in the Gulf of Mexico, off a deserted island in south america, in Belize, Thailand, and Nicaragua and Costa Rica. I felt like I wanted my own gear that fits and works right every time - so I finally ordered Wildhorn Outfitters Seaview 180 after having kept an eye on it for a while.

Over the last few months I've tried out a few products from Wildhorn outfitters and I've walked away impressed every time. This time was no different.

After trying this mask I had one big regret - not ordering this mask a few months ago. I really wish I could have used it last month in Central America but I know I will definitely be bringing it on my trip to Belize next year. Here's why:

Pros:

Visibility - It's hard to describe how amazing the visibility is in this mask. It is a completely different experience than any other snorkel equipment that I have ever used.

Breathing - With this mask the breathing experience is totally different. I'm not worried about breathing at all - which is kind of weird. When snorkeling I usually have to think about how I breathe - through my mouth and not my nose - keeping a tight seal around the mouthpiece - making sure not to breathe in too late after going under the water... you get the idea. With this mask I felt so much more comfortable and normal. Because the mask covers your entire face you can breathe out of mouth or nose. Also, if you try to breathe in when submerged no water actually enters your mask. You feel the pull of trying to breathe in without air but that's it. Also, if you get water in your mask the water will drain out the bottom of the mask when you lift your head out of the water.

Fog - When I tried the mask on at my house it fogged up a little but when I actually got in the water I had no issues with fog. I was planning on purchasing some anti-fog spray but now I think I'll delay that purchase and see if I actually need it in the future.

Go Pro Mount - I've used wrist mounts and other types of chest, head, and handheld mounts with a GoPro before and none of them really capture the footage how I want when snorkeling. I often spend too much time adjusting the head mount to make sure it's filming what I want it to film. With this setup I can set it up just how I want it and not worry about it being in the way or not being aimed the right way. Adjustment is also quick and easy.

Ease of use - This is the easiest snorkel mask I've ever used. It is a little shocking how quickly I got used to it. My young daughters would absolutely love masks of their own.

Cons:

Facial hair - You do need to be aware of how much facial hair you have when using this mask. Sometimes when I travel abroad I don't bother to bring a razor but with this mask I would probably bring one. Since the mask covers your entire nose and mouth it works better when I have recently shaved.

Overall:
If you snorkel regularly or are thinking of picking up equipment for your first snorkel adventure I can't recommend this mask more highly. I can't wait to use my mask again.
text_fidelity_b: Seaview 180 Degree Panoramic Snorkel Mask- Full Face Design,Panoramic Teal,Large/Extra Large

text_fidelity_a:
Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer Download the manual from the Burley website.

This is our second Travoy trailer. The other is still in use after 10 years. The new Travoy has some substantial upgrades:

• The new “kickstand” design keeps the trailer upright when parked with a load. The old one would tip over.
• New seatpost hitch allows a single hitch to be shared among two or more bikes. With the old one you had to buy more hitches.
• The tow arm now extends to accommodate rear bike racks and larger MTB wheels.
• Tow arm is now padded with foam for hand comfort.

The entire time we owned our first Travoy we mistakenly believed we should have chosen a flatbed instead. We recently bought a flatbed and don’t use it; bought a second Travoy as a backup. If all you do is local errands the Travoy is by far the easiest and best. If you tour or travel dirt roads a flatbed might be a better choice but you should want both a flatbed plus the Travoy because the Travoy is easier for local errands which are far more common.

The bags that are dedicated for use with the Travoy are costly and do not hold enough. Instead, wheel your Travoy into Target or Walmart and choose the largest clothes hamper that fits the Travoy form factor (see photo). Attach that hamper with three ratcheting tie-downs or four high quality, ADJUSTABLE bungees. Do not skimp on quality or number.

PROS:
• Lightweight, 10lbs +/-
• No tools or setup required. Screw the hitch onto your seatpost with the T-bold and you’re done.
• Folds to easily fit in a backseat, a trunk or an airline overhead.
• Holds up to $125 in groceries with the large hamper attached. Mind the maximum weight restriction (60lbs) and pack the heaviest items at the bottom (66% of load) and lighter items at the top (33%).
• With the Travoy you don’t have to bend over quite as far to reach cargo.
• Comes with a storage/carrying bag (although it’s mostly useless for carrying cargo).

CONS:
• You must adjust your riding style slightly. The Travoy is stable on level pavement but may tip over at significant road imperfections or surface debris. Slow down and approach handicapped ramps and driveways exactly at 90 degrees (perpendicular) to avoid catching a wheel on their raised shoulders. Avoid potholes and debris entirely. You’ll grow accustomed to this over time and it will not bother you. If the Travoy DOES tip, it doesn’t take the bike with it.
• If you run with the stock tires and tubes be prepared for flats. The availability of high quality 12.5” inch tires and tubes is extremely limited. All the tires from Asia that we tried are no good, even dangerous. We found very high quality 12.5 inch tires from the German manufacturer “Schwalbe” (available here on Amazon). Schwalbe currently offers the “Road Cruiser” for street and the “Black Jack” for trails and off-road (12/2020).
• 12.5” thorn resistant tubes are available here on Amazon but the Travoy 12.5 inch wheels require a 45 degree valve; otherwise there is not enough room to attach a pump or even a pump hose. These thorn resistant tubes had straight valves. To accommodate this shortcoming we found a "Air Inflator Hose Adapter" here on Amazon. Although it just barely fits, we can use it with both our floor pump and our road pump.

TIPS:
• In addition to thorn resistant tubes, we use the “Mr. Tuffy”-brand tire inserts on all our bike and trailer wheels (here on Amazon). Flats are now a very rare occurrence and we ride among numerous desert thorns.
• When using the hamper it is easy to cut a neon yellow reflective vest into three sections (left front, right front and back) and attach the sections to the hamper (left side, right side and rear, see photo).
• Reflective flags and flagpoles with mounts that fit your hamper are available here on Amazon. The flagpole we bought is high enough so that the flag can be seen above the level of a parked car (see photo). For added safety we now use this flag and pole on our bikes even without the trailer.
• When the hamper is inappropriate we use a cargo net. The cargo net is also handy if your hamper is overflowing.

Leave a comment if you have questions.
text_fidelity_b: Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer
